messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@crestline.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: baseline token rates & model catalog for hosted API

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking a look — I'm Samir on the infra/product side at Crestline. We're evaluating hosted inference vendors for an assistant product (realtime Q&A + brief summarization). Before we set up a live demo, could you send your standard hosted API rate card framed per 1M tokens, explicitly splitting input vs output rates? A few specific asks: 

- A concise table of input and output rates per 1M tokens across the model tiers you support (fast/low-cost, balanced, high-quality).
- The list of models available on the hosted tier today (including quantized variants if applicable).
- Any volume/commit discount thresholds and how streaming or function-calling affects accounting.
- Any minimum commit or contract term required to access higher discounts.

For context: our prototype currently sends ~200k messages/day; average prompt ~60 tokens in and ~120 tokens out. I've attached a short usage snapshot so you can map discounts to rough monthly totals.

Can you get that to me by EOD tomorrow? Also, if you have a one-pager or short pricing PDF, that would be great.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Crestline Analytics
procurement@crestline.ai
Attachment: crestline-usage-snapshot.csv (CSV)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@crestline.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: baseline token rates & model catalog for hosted API

Hi Samir — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the snapshot; that helps. Below is a compact baseline for hosted API IO pricing and the current model roster. I included notes on discounts and function-calling. If you'd like, I can convert this into a single-slide PDF.

Baseline hosted API pricing (per 1M tokens) — list is input / output:
- Fast tier (rw-sparrow-7b): 8 USD / 16 USD
- Balanced tier (rw-boreal-13b): 22 USD / 44 USD
- High-quality tier (rw-odin-70b fp16): 70 USD / 140 USD
- Quantized variant (rw-odin-70b int8): 36 USD / 72 USD

Notes:
- Streaming responses are billed on output tokens as they are emitted; function calls count both the input that invoked the function and the output returned by the tool.
- Embeddings and reranking are priced separately (I can include those rates if relevant).

Volume & commit discounts (hosted):
- 10% off at >= 50M tokens/mon (applies automatically when billed usage hits threshold)
- 20% off at >= 200M tokens/mon (or via quarterly prepay)
- Custom pricing available for >500M tokens/mon or multi-year commitments — requires a short procurement review.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved) is an alternative: flat monthly commit with predictable throughput and deeper discounts; we can discuss numbers if you prefer a committed pool.

Model roster (hosted today):
- rw-sparrow-7b (fast, FP16)
- rw-boreal-13b (balanced)
- rw-odin-70b (FP16 & quantized int8 variants)
- third-party: meta-ggml-13b (community), llama2-13b (licensed) — availability subject to regional/legal constraints

Attachments & links: I uploaded a short pricing sheet and added a starter HubSpot deal for Crestline for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/CST-2026-042. I've also attached a compact CSV mapping your snapshot to monthly token totals and estimated monthly spend under each tier.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Quick 30-min sync to confirm the target latency/throughput SLOs and whether function-calls/streaming are core to your flows.
2) If volume looks like >=200M tokens/mo, we prepare a simple commit proposal (1–3 quarters).
3) If you want to trial, we can spin a short-lived Dedicated pool for pilot workloads.

Lauren is cc'd — she owns commercial for this region and can surface any promo credits or timing constraints.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call today or tomorrow morning PT.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0122
Redwood Inference

Jonas — this is perfect, thanks.

A few quick clarifications: 
- Our production expectation is ~6M tokens/month initially, scaling to ~80–120M over 9–12 months if the pilot proves out.
- Function-calling will be used (we parse short structured responses and sometimes call external tools), so please assume both sides will be billed.
- Latency target: p95 < 350ms for short prompt/response pairs; will the fast tier meet that in us-west region?

Can we do a 30-minute sync Wednesday morning PT to run through commit options and timeline for a pilot Dedicated pool? After that call procurement will likely ask for an initial 3-month estimate for budget.

Thanks again — attaching a slightly expanded usage.csv for clarity.

—Samir
